authority.instrument: Maine Emergency Medical Dispatch Priority Reference System (Maine Board of EMS / Emergency Services Communication Bureau), §II.2 Protocol Requirements

provenance.source: Maine Board of Emergency Medical Services / Maine Emergency Services Communications Bureau, 'Emergency Medical Dispatch Priority Reference System', §II.2, pp. 1–3
provenance.notes: Maine adopts MPDS® as its statewide protocol (§II.1.A) — none of that proprietary content is reproduced here or anywhere in this project. What is encoded is only §II.2, Maine's own public-law list of what an approved protocol must contain, issued by a state board under 32 M.R.S.A. §85-A. Requirement wording is condensed from the rule's own numbered items and cited item by item. The direct document URL was not recorded at retrieval; re-verify against Maine EMS's published EMD documents before citing publicly.

requirements.text: Dispatch Life Support Protocols: physician-reviewed and approved, up to date, with proven validity and reliability.

check.note: medical review and approval is a property of the adopting agency

requirements.text: Categorical questioning of all callers.
requirements.notes: Checked as: a case-entry sequence asked on every call, before any protocol is selected.

requirements.text: Verification of the incident location.
Verification of the call-back number.
Nature of the call.
requirements.notes: Checked as: a case-entry question whose answer selects the protocol.

requirements.text: Consciousness of the patient(s) (Yes / No).
Breathing status of the patient(s).
Approximate age of patient(s).
requirements.notes: The rule's item 7 runs age and gender together on one line; they are scored separately here.

requirements.text: Gender of patient.
Proximity of caller to patient.
Additional, complaint-specific questions as indicated by the nature of the call and as directed by the protocol.
Medical case questions that emphasize symptoms.
Differentiation of agonal respirations, with questions that maximize the EMD's ability to decipher whether breathing is compatible with life.

patterns: breathing normally|normal breathing|respira normal|respire normalement|agonal|gasp|barely breathing

requirements.text: Trauma case questions that emphasize mechanism.
Trauma criteria clearly defined and in accordance with approved and national guidelines, including mechanisms of injury such as long falls.
requirements.notes: Checked as: the pack asks about fall height or distance, the rule's own example of a defined trauma criterion.

requirements.text: The protocol identifies circumstances that necessitate special rescue.
Method for assigning relative priority to calls that may affect level of response.
Capacity to select the appropriate number, nature, and mode of responding units.
requirements.notes: A pack expresses this through its response taxonomy; whether those levels map onto an agency's actual apparatus is a local configuration question outside the pack.

requirements.text: Scripted and systematic pre-arrival instructions as necessary, including directing bystanders to provide medical aid as indicated.
Prevention of further injury to patient(s), bystander(s), and responders.

patterns: if it is safe|stay safe|safe location|do not (attempt|touch)|no (intente|toque)|en s[ée]curit|ne (touchez|tentez)

requirements.text: Typically do not move the patient.

patterns: do not move|not to move|no (lo |la )?mueva|no mover|ne (le |la )?d[ée]placez|ne pas d[ée]placer

requirements.text: Evacuate the patient, the caller, and anyone else in immediate danger, case by case (e.g. carbon monoxide poisoning).

patterns: get out of the (house|building)|evacuate|leave the scene|salga|sal(ir|gan) de|[ée]vacu|quittez

requirements.text: Assess for hazards on or around the scene.
Ongoing assessment of patient status.

patterns: call me back|condition changes|watch (the|for)|llame(me)? de nuevo|si cambia|rappelez|surveillez

requirements.text: Medical management: cardio-pulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and automatic external defibrillator (AED).
requirements.notes: Scored as two patterns — CPR instructions and AED instructions — so a pack with telephone CPR but no AED script reads as partial, which is the honest result.

requirements.text: Medical management: foreign-body airway obstruction (FBAO) removal.
Medical management: bleeding control via direct pressure and elevation.
Medical management: keep the patient warm.
Medical management: childbirth instructions.

patterns: childbirth|contraction|deliver the baby|\bin labor\b|\bparto\b|dar a luz|accouch

requirements.text: Medical management: medication administration instructions (e.g. Epi-Pen).
Particular phrases available for use in repetitive persistence.
requirements.notes: Repetitive persistence is a technique — the same reassurance re-read until the caller acts. The engine's nearest facility is the persona's clarify-and-re-ask, which re-reads the pack's own clarify string; a pack cannot today carry a dedicated persistence phrase set.

check.note: no per-instruction persistence phrasing in the pack schema; the engine re-reads the clarify string instead

requirements.text: Post-dispatch instructions: identification of the incident location (e.g. turning on outside lights).

patterns: outside light|porch light|turn on .*light|watch for the (emergency )?unit|flag|prenda .*luz|allumez

requirements.text: Post-dispatch instructions: locking up pets.
Post-dispatch instructions: unlocking doors and/or providing key holder information.

patterns: unlock|open the door|key holder|abra la puerta|d[ée]verrouill|ouvrez la porte

requirements.text: Post-dispatch instructions: gathering medications.
Post-dispatch instructions: scene preservation.

patterns: do not (disturb|move) (the )?(scene|anything)|disturb the scene|no (toque|mueva) (nada|la escena)|ne (touchez|d[ée]placez) (rien|pas la sc[èe]ne)

requirements.text: Post-dispatch instructions: asking whether the patient is under a doctor's care, or whether there are doctor's instructions for the condition.
Per ASTM guidelines, the EMD system includes access to mass casualty plans, a directory of emergency response resources, and a description of the communications system configuration.

check.note: centre-level reference material, not protocol content

requirements.text: Record-keeping system, in accordance with the approved Quality Assurance program.

check.note: a centre system requirement; see §III for the QA/QI program it serves

requirements.text: Must meet or exceed the NHTSA-defined thirty-two chief complaint types.
